text.p: CompuServe Corp President Bob Massey on Friday said the online provider's financial position had improved since last summer, though he declined to forecast when it might return to profitability.

H&R Block Inc, which owns 80 percent of the company, postponed a planned spin-off of CompuServe in August because of its disappointing results and what Block described as market uncertainties in the online industry.
"Clearly, the financial position of CompuServe has strengthened," Massey said in an interview.

CompuServe's stock was up 5/16 to 10-1/2 in late afternoon trading on the Nasdaq, well below its all-time high of 35-1/2. The shares were priced at $30 each in their initial public offering last April.
Analysts on average expect CompuServe to post a loss of $0.74 a share for the fiscal year ending in April, according to a First Call survey. The company earned $0.66 a share the previous year.
Massey declined to comment on the fiscal 1997 estimates.

Salomon Brothers analyst Marc Usem said it was difficult to forecast how well the company would perform because it had shifted its focus to target business customers. But he said he thought profits would resume early in calendar 1998.
Last year, the Columbus, Ohio-based company withdrew its WOW! family-oriented online service in order to concentrate on business customers and more profitable consumer segments.
Kenneth Leon, an analyst with ABN AMRO - Chicago Corp, said, the firm was forecasting that CompuServe would break even in the July quarter, its first in the next fiscal year.

AOL, with eight million subscribers, has been beset with access problems since December, when it switched to charging a flat monthly fee to all customers. CompuServe has about five million subscribers (including a Japanese licensee's customers).
"Our contention is that we cannot make a profit by the flat pricing model, and I don't think anyone else in the industry can make money at this point in time with flat rate pricing," Massey said.
He said new orders rose fivefold after an advertising campaign that touted CompuServe's reliability.
In addition, CompuServe's corporate data network services, whose customers include the Visa International credit card group and Federal Express Corp, are "extremely profitable, ABN AMRO's Leon said.
Massey said CompuServe handles over one billion credit card authorizations a year.
